types.name: Context
types.meaning: One representable, fully supplied CommandBoundaryContext with finite ordered authentication and route resolver lists and a candidate command.
types.domain: The owner-accepted normally evaluated command-boundary input domain.

types.name: AuthOccurrence
types.meaning: A nonempty global carrier containing one distinct pair (context, zero-based list position) for every valid authentication-list entry, plus nonmember ghost elements when needed for ordinary nonempty FOL sorts.
types.domain: All interpreted Context values; position identity does not collapse equal row values.

types.name: RouteOccurrence
types.meaning: A nonempty global carrier containing one distinct pair (context, zero-based list position) for every valid route-list entry, plus nonmember ghost elements when needed for ordinary nonempty FOL sorts.
types.domain: All interpreted Context values; position identity does not collapse equal row values.

types.name: String
types.meaning: Exact string values including the empty string; no trimming, case folding, wildcard or coercion.
types.domain: The selected typed command-boundary string fields.

types.name: Bool
types.meaning: Exactly true or false for trust and completeness fields.

types.name: DecisionValue
types.meaning: Exactly two distinct values READY and DENY for the pure command-boundary outcome.
types.domain: Not the downstream authorization service's outcome.

predicates.name: AuthMember(c,a)
predicates.meaning: True exactly when a denotes one valid position in c's complete authentication resolver list; false for ghosts and foreign-context positions.

predicates.name: RouteMember(c,r)
predicates.meaning: True exactly when r denotes one valid position in c's complete route resolver list; false for ghosts and foreign-context positions.

predicates.name: QA(c,a)
predicates.meaning: AuthMember(c,a) and evidence_ref(a) equals c.request.authentication_evidence_ref, evidence_ref(a) and session_id(a) are nonempty, and trusted(a) is true; every field belongs to the same a.
predicates.domain: Context x AuthOccurrence; must be expanded or constrained by exact typed biconditional axioms in the canonical claim.

predicates.name: QR(c,r)
predicates.meaning: RouteMember(c,r) and route_id(r) equals c.request.route_id, route_id(r) and scope_evidence_ref(r) are nonempty, complete(r) is true, and required_permission resource, action and scope are each nonempty; every field belongs to the same r.
predicates.domain: Context x RouteOccurrence; must be expanded or constrained by exact typed biconditional axioms in the canonical claim.

predicates.name: InScopeNormal(c)
predicates.meaning: True for every Context in the fixed fully supplied representable finite-list carrier; never chosen after observing an implementation result. Normal completion of the selected evaluator is a separate correspondence obligation, not a filter on Context.
predicates.domain: Context; extension is the entire Context carrier.

predicates.name: Decision(c)
predicates.meaning: Abstract pure command-boundary outcome function into DecisionValue; an external correspondence binding may map it to selected typed evalOperation only under exact source and proof assumptions.

equality_rules: Authentication and route occurrence identity is (context identity, list position), so equal row values at different positions are unequal occurrences.
String and Bool comparisons use exact typed equality; nonempty means unequal to the exact empty string.

Candidate permission provenance compares resource, action and scope separately against the same unique qualifying route occurrence; candidate session compares against the same unique qualifying authentication occurrence.
READY and DENY are distinct and exhaust DecisionValue. A final downstream DENY is not the pure kernel DENY.
quantifiers: The decision proposition quantifies over every Context in the fixed complete finite-list carrier; InScopeNormal is true throughout that carrier, not an arbitrary subdomain.
Exactly one qualifying authentication or route row quantifies over occurrence positions, with existence and universal uniqueness over the same typed carrier.
The same bound qualifying occurrences witness candidate provenance inside their quantifier scopes; a separate nonqualifying row cannot supply values.

The occurrence carriers are nonempty even when one or both lists are empty; ghosts are excluded by membership, and field projections are total with arbitrary nonmember values that cannot affect qualification.
time_model: One pure command-boundary evaluation; the accepted rule has no clock, expiry, temporal transition, or changing resolver snapshot inside that evaluation.
currentness_rules: Complete resolver lists and the candidate belong to one evaluation context; later or stale resolver outputs cannot be silently spliced into it.
The source-bound typed/Rust/wrapper correspondence and its assumptions are separate from this business interpretation; source drift invalidates that evidence, not the business meaning.
Changing any qualifier, occurrence identity, scope condition or decision codomain requires a new reviewed meaning/model version.
applicability: fully supplied representable CommandBoundaryContext with complete finite resolver lists preserving multiplicity
normally evaluated pure command-boundary decision before downstream authorization
assumptions: Each valid list position maps injectively to exactly one occurrence and all valid entries are represented; ghosts and foreign-context positions are nonmembers.
All formal field projection functions are total on their nonempty carriers; values on nonmembers cannot satisfy a qualifying predicate without membership.

The selected pure typed evaluator's totality for the representable finite-list domain is a separate correspondence proof obligation and does not narrow InScopeNormal after observing implementation behavior.
QA and QR may be abbreviations only when their complete defining formulae are included in the exact canonical claim theory or expanded in the proposition.
The abstract Decision function is not defined by the generated Rust, selected Lean evaluator, or downstream authorization result.

The accepted DENY-without-downstream-call business fact is unqualified; the selected R5 proof counts only one direct wrapper call site and is insufficient by itself to establish the full no-call fact.
excluded_cases: missing resolver output, partial context, exceptions and nontermination outside the selected normal-evaluation claim
downstream authorization ALLOW or DENY semantics; direct-call-count proof alone does not establish the full no-downstream-call business fact
set conversion, deduplication, or value-based uniqueness of resolver rows
production deployment, provider behavior, EVF pass, F5 satisfaction and runtime_guarantees_observed
witnesses: A nonempty request ID, one fully qualifying authentication position, one fully qualifying route position and candidate fields copied from those same positions yield pure READY.
Two equal qualifying authentication entries at positions 0 and 1 yield pure DENY; equal values do not merge occurrence identities.
A context with both resolver lists empty remains in scope and yields pure DENY while formal occurrence sorts remain nonempty via nonmembers.
counterexamples: Treating a qualifying row value as the uniqueness identity collapses equal duplicate entries and wrongly permits READY.
Using a second matching but nonqualifying row to satisfy candidate provenance wrongly permits READY.
Defining InScopeNormal from observed successful results makes an incorrect or nonterminating implementation disappear from the obligation.
Interpreting Decision(c) as the downstream authorization result confuses kernel READY followed by downstream DENY with kernel DENY and zero direct calls.
Replacing the accepted no-downstream-call fact with a count of one direct wrapper call site silently weakens the business meaning.
vacuity_checks: Exhibit at least one in-scope READY context and one in-scope DENY context under the exact interpretation.
Exhibit an in-scope empty-list context, an equal-duplicate context, and a wrong-provenance context without narrowing InScopeNormal.
Check that READY and DENY are distinct/exhaustive and that both biconditional directions reject always-READY and always-DENY behavior.
claim_ceiling: Candidate occurrence-based InterpretationModel against the accepted v1 Auth meaning. No model acceptance, definitions-bearing v2 acceptance, current FormalClaim, admitted projection, TDE result, EVF/F5 pass or runtime_guarantees_observed.
